eval_prompt: Find GitHub documentation for privately published GitHub Pages sites. Determine which account or organization plans support them, how access is controlled, and whether site visibility can be limited to people with repository access.
success_criteria: Cite official access-control and plan restrictions.
Distinguish a private source repository from a privately accessible Pages site.
Do not promise repository membership enforcement without documentation.

title: Discover investigation and postmortem agent skills
eval_prompt: Find 5–10 reusable public agent skills for incident investigation/debugging and writing strong incident postmortems. Locate the actual SKILL.md files, compare their workflows and evidence requirements, and identify provenance, license, and maintenance status.
success_criteria: Link to actual readable SKILL.md files in canonical repositories.
Cover investigation and postmortem writing with specific comparison criteria.
Avoid counting mirrors or renamed copies as distinct designs.

title: Production precedent for explicit Go garbage collection
eval_prompt: Find documented examples of Go applications explicitly calling runtime.GC(). Explain the circumstances, motivation, and tradeoffs using concrete source call sites and maintainer discussions, and distinguish production code from tests or benchmarks.
success_criteria: Find verifiable production call sites and trace why they are invoked.
Use authoritative runtime documentation to contextualize costs and guarantees.
Exclude tests and benchmarks from the production precedent count.

title: Private planning preparation needs authenticated sources
eval_prompt: Prepare me for an upcoming planning meeting using my last week of private meeting notes, GitHub activity, Slack conversations, calendar, and Google Drive documents.
success_criteria: Identify required authenticated/private connectors.
Do not claim to have retrieved private meeting notes or Slack messages using a public web index.
